findings.current:
Jeok Cheongang was already out of the fight. If I expended any more strength here…

Then something truly irreversible would happen.
findings.defect: The draft changes the implied subject from Jeok Cheongang to Taekyung, making Taekyung’s further exertion the cause of the irreversible consequence.
findings.rationale: The surrounding sentences explicitly concern Jeok Cheongang’s incapacitation and the danger of him consuming any more strength.
findings.replacement: Jeok Cheongang was already out of the fight. If he expended any more strength here… then something truly irreversible would happen.
findings.source: 적천강은 이미 전투 불능이다. 여기서 더 힘을 소모한다면…… 그때는 정말 돌이킬 수 없는 일이 벌어질 것이다.

findings.current: I slowly drew up the less-than-ten-percent of my internal energy that remained.
findings.defect: The hyphenated nominal phrase is unidiomatic English.
findings.rationale: 일 할도 채 남지 않은 means that not even ten percent remains.
findings.replacement: I slowly drew up what little remained of my internal energy—not even ten percent.
findings.source: 나는 이제 일 할도 채 남지 않은 공력을 천천히 끌어 올렸다.

findings.current: “Go fuck yourself. After today, I’ll have nothing more to do with a bastard like you.”
findings.defect: The generic insult loses both the explicit dick-eating image and the mock-polite register of 잡수십쇼.
findings.rationale: The source deliberately combines strong vulgarity with exaggerated polite wording for comic contempt.
findings.replacement: “Why don’t you eat a dick, sir? After today, I’ll never have to deal with a bastard like you again.”
findings.source: “좆이나 까 잡수십쇼. 너 같은 새끼랑은 오늘을 마지막으로 상종할 일 없으니까.”

findings.current: “Who was it that said this? Once is coincidence. Twice is fate. A third meeting is destiny.”
findings.defect: Rendering 인연 as “fate” collapses the deliberate progression from coincidence to a connection or bond and finally to destiny.
findings.rationale: The ensuing exchange repeatedly contrasts 인연 with 운명, so they must remain distinct in English.
findings.replacement: “Who was it that said this? Once is coincidence. Twice is a connection. A third meeting is destiny.”
findings.source: “누가 그런 말을 했었지. 한 번은 우연. 두 번은 인연. 세 번째 만남은 운명이라고.”

findings.current: “Perhaps. It isn’t a relationship between a man and a woman, but if we’ve crossed paths twice in this vast world, wouldn’t that qualify as fate?”
findings.defect: The line again renders 인연 as “fate,” erasing the distinction that drives the Blood Lord’s wordplay.
findings.rationale: He is classifying their second encounter as 인연, not yet as the 운명 reserved for a third meeting.
findings.replacement: “Perhaps. It isn’t a relationship between a man and a woman, but if we’ve crossed paths twice in this vast world, wouldn’t that make it a connection?”
findings.source: “글쎄. 남녀관계는 아니지만, 이 드넓은 천하에서 두 번이나 마주쳤다면 인연 정도는 되지 않을까?”

findings.current: “Oh, what about that Third Rate sect called the Mount Heng Sword Sect? Is it still around? I heard a report from one of my subordinates that you killed the Sect Leader’s son. I lost interest after Eight Spring Gorge, so I haven’t paid much attention.”
findings.defect: The draft invents Taekyung as the killer and turns an unspecified Sect Leader’s son into a definite individual.
findings.rationale: The Korean does not identify Taekyung as the subject of 죽였다는; it reports only that a son of the Sect Leader was killed.
findings.replacement: “Oh, what about that Third Rate sect called the Mount Heng Sword Sect? Is it still around? I did hear from one of my subordinates that one of its Sect Leader’s sons had been killed. I lost interest after Eight Spring Gorge, so I haven’t paid much attention.”
findings.source: “아, 항산검문인가 하는 그 삼류 문파는 아직 남아 있나? 아랫놈에게 문주의 아들놈 하나를 죽였다는 보고를 듣긴 했는데. 팔천협 이후로는 영 관심이 안 생겨서 말이야.”

findings.current: “Once is coincidence. Twice is fate. A third meeting is destiny. What do you think? Wouldn’t the two of us qualify as fate?”
findings.defect: Both occurrences of 인연 are translated as “fate,” making the contrast with 운명 semantically incoherent.
findings.rationale: The Blood Lord is still calling their two encounters an 인연 while reserving 운명 for a third.
findings.replacement: “Once is coincidence. Twice is a connection. A third meeting is destiny. What do you think? Wouldn’t you say there’s a connection between us?”
findings.source: “한 번은 우연. 두 번은 인연. 세 번은 운명이라고. 어때, 우리 정도면 인연이 아닐까?”

findings.current: “You know that bullshit about once being coincidence, twice being fate, or whatever?”
findings.defect: The paraphrase repeats the same loss of distinction between 인연 and the following 운명.
findings.rationale: Taekyung’s next line proposes skipping the intermediate 인연 stage and going directly to 운명, which requires distinct English terms.
findings.replacement: “You know that bullshit about once being coincidence, twice making a connection, or whatever?”
findings.source: “한 번은 우연. 두 번은 인연. 어쩌구 하는 그 개소리 말인데.”

findings.current: When Shanxi’s martial world staggered, the mounted bandits of Gaoyuan rose up.
findings.defect: The draft misses the binding term “Murim,” while “rose up” suggests an uprising rather than the bandits running rampant.
findings.rationale: 무림 maps to “Murim,” and 발호했다 describes unchecked predation or rampant activity.
findings.replacement: When Shanxi’s Murim reeled, the mounted bandits of Gaoyuan ran rampant.
findings.source: 산서 무림이 휘청이자 고원의 마적들이 발호했다.

findings.current: He wanted to collapse and give up.
findings.defect: “And give up” adds an explicit surrender impulse absent from the source.
findings.rationale: 쓰러지고 싶다 expresses only the desire to fall or collapse; it does not state that Cheongpung wants to surrender.

findings.current: The Blood Lord shook his head, his face pale with exhaustion.
findings.defect: The draft changes the Blood Lord’s appalled or fed-up reaction to Jin Taekyung’s tenacity into physical exhaustion.
findings.rationale: 질린 얼굴 describes being aghast, sickened, or fed up; his physical condition is conveyed separately by the blood covering his body and his rough breathing.
findings.replacement: The Blood Lord shook his head, looking thoroughly appalled.
findings.source: 질린 얼굴로 고개를 내젓는 혈주 역시 전신이 피범벅이었다.

findings.current: “Have I gone insane, or are you people…”
findings.defect: The idiom is mistranslated as the Blood Lord questioning his own sanity rather than calling the others lunatics.
findings.rationale: 이런 미친놈들을 봤나 is an incredulous reaction to the other people’s madness.

findings.defect: “Broken through your shell” is an unnatural collocation and weakens the image of escaping a limiting shell.
findings.rationale: The line metaphorically marks Cheongpung overcoming the fear that confined him; “broken free of” preserves that image naturally.

summary: Two critical subject changes alter who expends strength and who killed the Sect Leader’s son. The draft also collapses the repeated distinction between connection and destiny, loses a profane register joke, and contains several localized characterization and terminology errors.
